contributions.text:
Asked: a last pass to tighten the mana on b3-v1 (35 lands, lands-only W 19 / U 29, with rocks W 23 / U 33; on-curve lands-only W 0.548 / U 0.804; mana-fit short W 13, U 3 against 36/36). The white figure is mostly an instrument step, not a hole that opened: the pre-Concealment list reads effective_pips 1 and a W target of 22 (on-curve 0.866); Clever Concealment is the fifth double-W card among 22 white cards (Austere Command, Clever Concealment, Guardian of Faith, Heliod, Supreme Verdict — enumerated from the branch cards.json), the 20% quorum is five, so effective_pips became 2 and the same 19 Plains-side lands now score against WW-by-turn-3 (36 sources, which no 35-land two-colour base can reach for both colours). 'Short by 13' is therefore a yardstick; but the requirement under it is real, because the commander himself is {2}{W}{W}: with the production hypergeometric, WW among the ten cards seen by turn 4 is 0.611 off lands and 0.728 with the four W rocks counted, so roughly one game in four cannot cast Heliod on curve without a mulligan or a tutor. Every single-card white fix moves lands-only W on-curve by exactly one source, 0.548 to 0.580 (WW by turn 4: 0.611 to 0.643); the options differ only in what blue and the pilot pay. The smallest change that tightens white and charges blue nothing is one land for one land: a basic Island out, Prismatic Vista in — untapped, fetches a basic Plains or Island with the hand in view, one life, blue stays at 29 land sources (0.804), lands stay at 35, Mystic Sanctuary keeps 15 other Islands. Island to Plains does the same for white free of charge but costs blue one source (0.804 to 0.785) and reverses one of the 13th's three Plains-to-Island moves, whose 'white over target' why was true under the 22 target and is not under the 36. The log (001, 002, 003) records no colour-screw: this pass is driven by instruments, not by a game.
